subject.title: [Feature]: Store configuration backup files in their own directory, with datetime name convention

question: Should core config backups move to a dedicated `config-backup/` directory with datetime names, or should OpenClaw keep adjacent backups and only change naming/docs?
rationale: The code change is feasible, but backup layout affects config recovery, sensitive backup permissions, legacy `.bak.N` retention, doctor docs, and overlapping timestamp-only work, so maintainers need to choose the canonical product contract before implementation.

options.title: Adopt Dedicated Directory Layout
options.body: Make this issue the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy adjacent backups, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and tests.

options.title: Limit Scope To Timestamp Suffixes
options.body: Keep backups adjacent and route the naming-only work through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39923 and its linked PR, then narrow or close this directory request separately.

options.title: Keep Current Backup Ring
options.body: Reject the layout change and document the adjacent numbered backup ring as the intended stable behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt Dedicated Directory Layout
recommendation.body: Make this issue the canonical design and require a migration-safe implementation covering legacy adjacent backups, recovery, permissions, retention, audit text, doctor docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history and discussion context on the config backup/recovery surface.
